messages:
Marina: paging oncall — p99 tail for streaming generation spiked to ~2.8s across prod (us-east-1) starting ~10:02 UTC, p95 sits ~420ms. Noticed a simultaneous drop in prefix-cache hit rate from ~92% to ~43% in the last 12m. Dash: https://dash.internal/redwood/streams?panel=tail_latency

oncall-bot: incident created INC-5753210000 severity=sev2 (auto). Paging Phil.

Phil: on it, thanks Marina. Can we confirm whether this aligns with the morning prefix-hash rollout? Any 5xx/500 spikes or is this pure tail latency?

Marina: no 5xx spike in SLOs, error rates flat. This looks like token-level tail latency causing some streaming sessions to exceed client timeouts (CS reported 3 customer timeouts so far). We see increased backend stalls in streaming workers and a drop in KV-prefetch hit_rate for prefix keys.

Devon: I was on the prefix hasher rollout earlier — we shipped prefix-hash v3 with salted buckets at 07:45 and ramped to 15% in us-east-1. Could be a mismatch in salt config or a partitioning edge-case.

Kevin: sharing quick metrics query outputs:
```
# recent 15m
prefix_cache.hit_rate{env=prod,region="us-east-1"}  -> 0.43
streaming.p99_latency_ms{env=prod,region="us-east-1"} -> 2800
kv.prefetch.queue_depth -> 120
worker.stream.tail.stall_count -> +480 (10m)
```

Marina: logs show many `cache.get` fallbacks to remote read with `key_namespace:null` and `prefix_lookup:miss`. Example trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d.

Phil: ok. First mitigation: stop the v3 rollout in us-east-1 and revert keys to v2 routing, kick a cache-warm job for hot prefixes. Who can flip the rollout flag? If infra can do quick rollback we should see hit-rate recovery.

infra-sre: rolling back now — calling admin API to set variant to v2 for region us-east-1.
```
POST https://admin.internal/rollouts/prefix-hash
{
  "env": "prod",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "variant": "v2",
  "percentage": 100
}
```
Applying change -> accepted. Warmup job queued (batch size 2000 prefixes).

incident-bot: rollout change detected: prefix-hash variant -> v2 for prod/us-east-1 by infra-sre. Noting in incident.

Kevin: after rollback (t+2m) seeing hit_rate climb: 43% -> 67% and p99 down to ~980ms. Still elevated but trending.

CS-ops: Confirmed with support: bigcustomerX reported timeout errors in their streaming connector at 10:06 UTC, they are being notified we're mitigating. No escalations to legal or billing yet.

Marina: performing follow-up checks: verifying cache invalidation window and TTL behavior. Likely root cause: v3 used salted prefix namespace that wasn't present in the warming index, so the hot set missed prefetches causing cold-shard reads and tail stalls.

Devon: noted. We'll lock rollout and add a gating check on warming coverage before any future prefix-hash rollouts. Also creating a postmortem ticket to evaluate canary sizing and prewarm guarantees.

Phil: immediate action items: (1) monitor p95/p99 for 30m and confirm p99 < 1s target, (2) CS to notify affected customers with a short summary, (3) infra to run a targeted prewarm for top 10k prefixes across regions, (4) Dev to add warming coverage check to rollout pipeline.

infra-sre: targeted prewarm started — coordinated job ID prewarm-575321. Current progress: 45% of prefixes queued.

Kevin: quick checklist for oncall handoff: what we changed, why, and next steps:
- Changed: reverted prefix-hash v3 -> v2 in prod/us-east-1 at 10:08 UTC
- Impact: p99 reduced from ~2.8s -> ~900ms in 5m; prefix hit_rate rising from 43% -> 68%
- Customer impact: three streaming timeouts reported; CS-ops notified customers; no 5xx spike
- Next: observe for 30m, complete prewarm, add gating to rollout pipeline, postmortem assigned (PM: Devon)

Phil: thanks team — I'll follow until p99 stays below 1s for 30m, then we'll close the live mitigation. Night oncall: @Marina will handoff at 18:00 UTC with notes above.

Marina: handoff noted. Saving logs and dashboards to incident timeline. If anyone needs me tonight DM. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-5753210000 updated: status=mitigated_trending. Next update scheduled in 15m.
